subject: Issues preparing movement data for model fitting

messages.author: bd4368f44a7010d6
messages.subject: Issues preparing movement data for model fitting
parts:
Hey Chris,


I am working with telemetry data of 18 white storks which have their breeding area in Loburg, Germany. The data features a default temporal interval of 5 mins which is, due to bad weather conditions, sometimes decreased to 20 minutes or even one hour intervals. Furthermore, every night, the devices shut down for 6 hours between around 8pm and 2am.


With the help of the ctmm package I would like to reconstruct the movement path in order to derive a more realistic value (including confidence intervals) of the time spent in certain areas of interest at each day during the breeding season in one specific year. The migration periods (autumn and spring) are already excluded from the data.


I attended the Animove summerschool in 2017 and followed the basic steps for data pre-processing provided in your introductory lesson. However, using the stork data I encountered several problems:


The data comes in movebank format featuring the necessary columns and naming conventions (location.long, location.lat, timestamp, etc) as well as the additional column eobs.horizontal.accuracy.estimate.

I tried the pre-processing workflow with different individuals, as a reproducible example however, I sent you the data of one month (April) from a single individual due to privacy reasons.


Step 1: Convert data to Telemetry object


The conversion seems to work but I am not sure whether the error estimate column is automatically recognized or if I have to specify it somehow when creating the telemetry object? I only found the UERE variable but don't know how to include it there. Here is my code example:


# convert dataframe with WGS84 coordinates to to Telemetry object with ETRS89 projection

StorkTele<- as.telemetry(Storks_samp, timezone ="UTC", timeformat= "%F %T",

projection = CRS('+proj=laea +lat_0=52 +lon_0=10 +x_0=4321000 +y_0=3210000 +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs'))


Step 2: Data cleaning


In a next step I tried to identify outliers using the outlie() function and got a dataframe with two columns (distance, speed).


OUT <- outlie(StorkTele)


Looking at the resulting values I noticed, that quite often, when the birds flew distances larger than zero between two consecutive locations the speed estimate remained zero. Intuitively, that seems to be wrong for me. Do you have an explanation for that?


Step 3: Inspect autocorrelation


In order to inspect the autocorrelation structure of my data I created and plotted a correlogram(). The creation worked but the plot() command produced the following warning:


CORR <- correlogram(StorkTele)

plot(CORR)


Warning message:
In atanh(SVF) : NaNs produced


… and resulted in an erroneous plot: (see Attachement_1_Correlogram_Error)


To inspect what causes the NaNs I did the following:


NaN <- cbind(CORR$SVF, atanh(CORR$SVF))


The problem seems to come from the CORR$SVF. The latter results in values slightly larger than 1 and produces the NaNs when calculating the hyperbolic tangent. Looking at my input coordinates I was wondering if that is a result from the number of decimal places of my coordinates taken into account when creating the telemetry object or if anything is seriously wrong with my data? Would you have an idea where the issue comes from and how I can fix it?


Thank you very much in advance for your help.


Greetings,

Ines

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Issues preparing movement data for model fitting
parts:
Hi Ines,

I hope you are well. A lot of this material is going to be in an upcoming paper that I am finalizing now. Some of this is presently in vignette('error').

1) This appears to be e-obs data and it imports with an error column which you can see from the head() or names() of the telemetry object, where you have HDOP and VAR.xy columns. You can also see from plot() that there are error circles of different size.

The calibration for e-obs data comes from Scott LaPoint's fisher calibration data, and I should warn that the collars that did not function well did not have the same calibration parameters (UEREs). You can use your own calibration data to overwrite this UERE value, following vignette('error').

2) The speed & distance estimators here are error informed, with the speed estimates derived from point-to-point distances (so they represent an upper bound on the true speed). These estimates consider the erroneous location observations as being distributed around the true locations by the specified error. As error inflates the "distance" between erroneous locations, accounting for error will estimate a smaller quantity. Interestingly, when the error is above a certain threshold, the point estimate of the true distance is zero. However, the full posterior distribution (CIs) includes more than zero. I do not return this information, though, because it is some work to calculate and I don't see the use for it in outlier detection.

3) correlogram() in ctmm is only for residuals. Other data will break assumptions in the math. If you want to check the residuals assuming an IID model, you can fit an IID model and then run that and the data through the residuals() function, and then the output residuals through correlogram(). If you want to inspect the autocorrelation structure of data, then variogram() function is better because its estimator is unbiased. Tell me if you have any issues with that.

Best,
Chris
